title: Speech titled: " Rhodes 1952-2026: from the "National Carteria" to the "Antikythera Mechanism" and beyond"
excerpt: The art and speech magazine Nisides organizes an event – speech – discussion on Saturday, November 28 at 18.30 in the hall of the Public Benefit Foundation
content:
CULTURE

  • The arts and literature magazine Nisides is organising a talk and discussion on Saturday 28 November at 18.30 at the Emmanouil and Mary Stamatiou Rhodes Scholarship Foundation.
  • Yannis Iraklidis will discuss the development of public art in Rhodes from 1952 to the present, examining its historical, ideological and political dimensions.
  • The talk will consider significant sculptures, from “Ethniki Karteria” and “Alexander Diakos” to more recent works and contemporary references to ancient Greek and Rhodian art.
  • The presentation will be accompanied by photographs and video footage of the unveiling of the “Alexander Diakos” monument in 1958. The introduction will be given by Fragkiskos Kalavasis, and Anastasia Zeppou will chair the event.

The arts and literature magazine Nisides is organising an event featuring a talk and discussion on Saturday 28 November at 18.30 in the hall of the Emmanouil and Mary Stamatiou Rhodes Scholarship Foundation (12 Grigori Lambraki Street, Rhodes).

The event’s keynote speaker will be Yannis Iraklidis, whose talk is entitled:

Rhodes 1952-2026: from “Ethniki Karteria” to the “Antikythera Mechanism” and beyond.

The adventures of art in public spaces.

The talk seeks to shed light on some aspects of the relationship that develops over time between a city and public art, focusing on Rhodes in the post-war decades. It traces the history of the installation of artworks in public spaces, the aims of those involved, and the ideological or political motives behind their initiatives. It also offers aesthetic and artistic assessments of some of the most significant sculptures encountered by people walking around the city.

The starting point is the beginning of the 1950s, when the Greek state, after integration, draws up a plan for de-Italisation in the cultural sector. As far as our subject is concerned, the importance of "National Karteria" and "Alexander Diakos" in this process is highlighted, as well as the controversies that accompany it, an interesting and rather unknown chapter of local history.

Particular attention is given to sculptures that have proliferated in the city, mainly since the 1990s, and which encompass a wide range of subjects: symbolic representations, statues, busts of politicians and other prominent figures, and decorative and artistic sculptural compositions.

The final part of the talk explores, from cultural, social and political perspectives, the phenomenon of looking back to the city’s collection of ancient Greek and Rhodian artworks, which serve as models for contemporary interventions, copies or adaptations in public spaces.

The talk is accompanied by extensive photographic material and a video showing footage of the unveiling of the “Alexander Diakos” monument in 1958.

The event will be introduced by Fragkiskos Kalavasis, Professor Emeritus at the University of the Aegean, who will set the talk’s theme in the context of the city’s complex relationship with culture today, when the image is more powerful than what it depicts.

The event and the discussion that follows will be chaired by teacher Anastasia Zeppou, a member of the editorial board of Nisides.
